title: Scalar and Vector Triple Products
notes: **Scalar triple product:** $\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c})$. It equals the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$.

**Properties:** $\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) = \vec{b} \cdot (\vec{c} \times \vec{a}) = \vec{c} \cdot (\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ (cyclic). If any two vectors are equal or parallel, the product is zero.
**Vector triple product:** $\vec{a} \times (\vec{b} \times \vec{c}) = (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})\vec{c}$. This expands a cross-of-cross into a linear combination.
**Applications:** scalar triple product gives volume; vector triple product appears in torque and angular momentum calculations and in simplifying vector expressions.
